subject: Davidson et al. (2024)
object: Davidson et al. (2024) described a 22-month-old Caucasian boy (P1) with non-consanguineous parents who was born at 31 weeks' gestation. At 4 days of age he developed peri-umbilical erythema with sterile neutrophilic inflammation around a urachal remnant. After surgery the wound dehisced and failed to close, and he later developed a spontaneous cutaneous duodenal stoma. At 8 weeks he had an acute respiratory deterioration with body edema, hypotension and presumed pulmonary edema that responded to corticosteroids. He had recurrent panniculitis, pathergy with sterile pustular abscesses at injection and cannula sites, a tricuspid valve echogenic focus treated as culture-negative endocarditis, raised CRP (100-200 mg/L), neutrophilia, monocytosis, eosinophilia, persistent thrombocytopenia, initial hypogammaglobulinemia, and a skin biopsy showing acute inflammatory exudate with suppuration and necrosis.

subject: Davidson et al. (2024)
object: Davidson et al. (2024) described a Saudi girl (P2) born at term to non-consanguineous parents. At 7 months of age, 2 weeks after routine vaccinations, she presented with fever, generalized edema and multiple tender skin lesions that progressed to cellulitis-like plaques and necrotizing fasciitis with ulceration requiring debridement and fasciotomy. She had leukocytosis, neutrophilia and a high CRP (264 mg/L), all cultures were negative, and biopsy showed neutrophil and plasma cell infiltration with necrosis. At 12 months she had a second attack with fever, erythematous plaques, CRP 393 mg/L and skin biopsy showing panniculitis, and she responded promptly to corticosteroids.

subject: Davidson et al. (2024)
object: In P1, trio exome sequencing by Davidson et al. (2024) identified a de novo heterozygous c.386G>C variant in the OTULIN gene, resulting in a cys129-to-ser (C129S) substitution. The variant was absent from gnomAD. Cys129 is part of the catalytic domain and is essential for OTULIN enzymatic activity.

subject: OTULIN c.385T>A / c.386G>C / p.C129S
Davidson et al. (2024)
object: In P2, whole-genome sequencing by Davidson et al. (2024) identified a heterozygous c.385T>A variant in the OTULIN gene that results in the same cys129-to-ser (C129S) substitution. Testing of the parents confirmed that it was de novo.

subject: Davidson et al. (2024)
object: Davidson et al. (2024) found that C129S OTULIN had thermostability similar to wildtype and that OTULIN and LUBAC component levels were normal in patient fibroblasts. However, the mutant failed to hydrolyze M1-linked di-ubiquitin. An activity-based probe showed that wildtype (active) and C129S (inactive) OTULIN were coexpressed in roughly equal amounts in patient fibroblasts. Surface plasmon resonance showed that C129S OTULIN bound M1-di-ubiquitin with high affinity.

subject: Davidson et al. (2024)
object: Davidson et al. (2024) observed accumulation of M1-linked ubiquitin chains in patient fibroblasts. Transfecting C129S OTULIN into HEK293T cells, which express endogenous OTULIN, caused M1-ubiquitin accumulation and dose-dependent NF-kappa-B activation. Wildtype OTULIN and the loss-of-function variants Y244C and N341D did not have these effects. C129S OTULIN drove NF-kappa-B activity even when cotransfected with wildtype at lower ratios, indicating a dominant negative effect.

subject: Davidson et al. (2024)
object: Davidson et al. (2024) found that C129S patient fibroblasts were as sensitive to TNF/cycloheximide-induced cell death as fibroblasts from patients with biallelic ORAS, and more sensitive than fibroblasts from OTULIN-haploinsufficient patients or healthy donors. The death was mainly apoptotic, because it was reduced by caspase inhibition and minimally affected by necrostatin-1. TNF-induced MAPK and NF-kappa-B signaling and IL-6/IL-8 secretion were largely normal in patient fibroblasts.

subject: Davidson et al. (2024)
object: Davidson et al. (2024) observed markedly increased transcription of IFNB1 and IL6, and to a lesser extent TNF, in PBMCs from P1. P1's fibroblasts had an elevated interferon-stimulated gene score that was similar to fibroblasts from patients with biallelic ORAS and higher than in healthy donor and OTULIN-haploinsufficient fibroblasts. THP-1 monocytes stably expressing C129S OTULIN, but not wildtype OTULIN, showed a similar inflammatory gene signature.

subject: Davidson et al. (2024)
object: Davidson et al. (2024) showed that C129S OTULIN binds LUBAC. In cells it promoted ubiquitination of LUBAC components SHARPIN and, to a lesser extent, HOIP. Patient fibroblasts showed increased OTULIN-LUBAC interaction, and most LUBAC-bound OTULIN was catalytically inactive. Patient cells also showed reduced recruitment of LUBAC (HOIP, SHARPIN) to the TNFR1 signaling complex and reduced RIPK1 modification. The authors concluded that accumulation of M1-ubiquitin on LUBAC reduces its recruitment to TNFR1 and promotes TNF-induced cell death, which leads to necrotizing tissue.

subject: Davidson et al. (2024)
object: Davidson et al. (2024) reported that both patients responded to corticosteroids. P1 was treated with adalimumab, which allowed steroid reduction, lowered CRP and supported wound healing; ruxolitinib was also tried in P1, but its benefit was unclear. P2 was treated with infliximab plus methotrexate, was weaned off steroids and remained in remission for 2 years. Prophylactic antibiotics improved wound healing in P1 and controlled recurrent chest infections in P2.

subject: Davidson et al. (2024)
object: Davidson et al. (2024) reported the first heterozygous, dominant negative OTULIN variant to cause ORAS-like disease. It arose de novo in 2 unrelated individuals, in contrast to the previously reported biallelic loss-of-function variants.
